body:
`cps/__init__.py` constructs the limiter with `key_func=True`. flask_limiter
expects a callable and stores it as `self._key_func`, handing it to every
limit that does not override it.

Every `@limiter.limit(...)` in the tree happens to pass its own `key_func`
today (13 callsites across `cps/web.py` and `cps/api/auth.py`), so nothing is
broken right now. The trap is the next one: a limit added without that kwarg
calls `True()`.

Measured against the shipped image, with a limit declared the obvious way:

    @lim.limit('3/minute')      # no key_func
    ...
    File ".../flask_limiter/extension.py", line 1077, in __evaluate_limits
        limit_key = lim.key_func()
    TypeError: 'bool' object is not callable
    status: 500

Rate limits here sit on login and token endpoints, so the failure surfaces as
a 500 on an auth route, and only for the person who added the limit correctly
by the library's own documentation.

Fix is a real callable — `get_remote_address` is the library's own default and
matches what most callsites already pass. Worth pairing with a test that
declares a limit without `key_func` and asserts it returns non-500, so the
fallback path has coverage it currently lacks.

Found while fixing #1443 (explicit limiter storage), which touched the same
constructor.
title: Global limiter key_func is the literal True, so any rate limit added without an explicit key_func 500s
